content:
maria: Hey team — hitting an odd issue in our .NET client when streaming responses from the Redwood API. After we added Polly retries and a short overall timeout, about 1 in 50 streaming requests hang forever (or until process restart). Anyone seen this?

raj: ugh. Are you creating a new HttpClient per request or using IHttpClientFactory?

maria: new HttpClient() per request in the code path that does streaming (legacy). We also configured Polly with WaitAndRetryAsync for transient failures and TaskCanceledException caused by timeouts. No special handler config.

sam: that immediately rings a bell — creating many HttpClient instances can exhaust sockets / cause weird connection reuse problems. Also retries + streaming is tricky because stream bodies aren't rewindable.

maria: yeah — I dug in and observed the request gets retried by Polly, but the second attempt stalls on SendAsync. Stack traces show waiting inside SocketsHttpHandler.

olivia: couple quick suggestions: (1) use IHttpClientFactory (AddHttpClient) so sockets are pooled correctly; (2) for streaming endpoints use HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead so the client doesn't buffer the whole response; (3) avoid automatic retry for non-idempotent/streaming requests.

maria: thanks. For (3) — how do we disable Polly for those calls but keep it for regular API calls?

raj: two options: register named/typed clients — one with retry policy, one without. Or use PolicyWrap and in code select NoOpPolicy for streaming calls. Example registration:```csharp
services.AddHttpClient("redwood-default")
  .AddPolicyHandler(retryPolicy);

services.AddHttpClient("redwood-streaming");
```

sam: also important: when you retry HttpRequestMessage, its Content stream may have been already consumed. Polly re-sends the same HttpRequestMessage instance by default which will fail or deadlock if the Content stream can't be re-read. You need to make the request content replayable (e.g., ByteArrayContent) or recreate the message per retry.

maria: our streaming requests are GETs (no request body) so the content reuse isn't the problem here — more like connection state and cancellation.

olivia: okay then check SocketsHttpHandler settings — PooledConnectionLifetime and PooledConnectionIdleTimeout can help avoid stale connections. Example:```csharp
services.AddHttpClient("redwood-streaming")
  .ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(() => new SocketsHttpHandler {
    PooledConnectionLifetime = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5),
    PooledConnectionIdleTimeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(120),
    KeepAlivePingPolicy = HttpKeepAlivePingPolicy.WithActiveRequests, // net7+ if used
  });
```

raj: also ensure you call SendAsync with ResponseHeadersRead:```csharp
using var resp = await client.SendAsync(req, HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead, ct);
resp.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
await using var body = await resp.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync(ct);
await body.CopyToAsync(targetStream, 81920, ct);
```

sam: small gotcha — if your timeout triggers cancellation while CopyToAsync is running, and Polly catches TaskCanceledException and retries, you can end up with multiple concurrent requests competing for connection slots. Policy should typically not retry on cancellations triggered by external CancellationToken for streaming. Filter which exceptions cause retry.

maria: good point. We're using a CancellationToken that comes from the request pipeline; I'll stop retrying for TaskCanceledException and only retry on HttpRequestException and transient 5xx.

olivia: also add logging around Dispose of the stream and response. If you forget to dispose the HttpResponseMessage/stream it can hold sockets open. Using 'await using' pattern helps.

maria: thanks all — action items for me: switch to IHttpClientFactory named client for streaming, set ResponseHeadersRead, tighten Polly rules (no retry on cancellation), add SocketsHttpHandler pooling config, and add extra logging for Dispose. I'll report back. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: deploy-checklist — make sure to run integ tests under load and watch socket counts (netstat) and connection pool metrics.

maria: will do. If I still see hangs I'll post back with a minimal repro. Appreciate the quick ideas!
